substitutes: No tow toy? A knotted old fleece strip or a soft towel that is gentle on teeth.
No signs? Use cushions as ports.
title: The Tugboat Adventure
clue: A tiny harbor, a strong tow-line and a manifest that only your dog can fill in.
reveal: For a dog who already loves tug. Your dog picks the cargo from three toys, hauls it across three very short crossings with a trade at every dock, then searches a customs shed of towel crates for it. Short, light and over while they still want more.
objective: Sail three very short tug crossings with a trade at every dock, then search the customs shed for the cargo your dog picked, and settle.
instructions: Check your crew. Only for a dog who already tugs in a loose, wiggly way, takes the toy gently and happily swaps it. If your dog stiffens, growls intensely, guards toys or has any mouth, neck or back concerns, skip to the Cargo edition or ask your vet.

Build the harbor on a non-slip floor in a cleared space: rugs or yoga mats on any slippery stretch, no stairs or furniture nearby. Mark three ports a few strides apart with paper signs or cushions. At the last port lay three folded towels (the crates), a flat folded blanket as a landing pad and a bowl of fresh water.

Fill in the manifest. Lay three of your dog's own toys low on the floor and let them nose around. Whichever one they pick up, nudge or sniff first is today's cargo: write it on the manifest card. If none interests them, sail another day. Put the other two toys away.
Invite your dog to sail. Hold the long soft tow toy still and low, near the floor, and let your dog take hold of it. If they do not, the voyage is canceled.

Crossing: when your dog takes hold, tug gently sideways (never up and down) with light resistance for only 10 to 15 seconds, two or three pulls. Then ease off and let them tow you a few steps toward the next port. Never lift your dog off the floor.

Docking: at each port, go still and quiet and show the cargo toy low. When your dog lets go, hand them the cargo and give a calm pause. Never pull the tow toy out of their mouth and never chase a dog who runs off with it. If they will not let go, stand still and be boring until they do or end the game. Repeat for all three crossings, with a sip of water and a few seconds to do nothing at every dock. Stop early at any sign they are losing interest, getting stiff or gripping hard.

Customs inspection at the last port: while your dog watches, tuck the cargo toy under one of the three towel crates and let them find it at their own pace. If they pick the wrong crate, lift the others gently to show nothing is under them. The nose game is the quiet landing.
Cast off. Coil the tow-line, hang it out of reach, write the number of crossings on the manifest and sit for a quiet minute on the landing pad together.
twist: Your dog chooses the cargo, every crossing ends in a trade, and the voyage lands in a customs search, so the excitement always has somewhere calm to go.
variations: Cargo edition, for a dog who prefers carrying to tugging: put out a basket of familiar toys (the Depot) and a mat a few steps away (the Post Office). Let your dog choose the cargo and where it goes, never take a toy from their mouth and stop after about five deliveries.
Seated owner: tow from a chair, keep the toy low and let your dog do the pulling.
Soft-mouth or small-space version: a fleece tow toy, a hallway harbor and a single crossing.
Shorter voyage: one or two ports is a full voyage.
completion: You have sailed the crossings your dog enjoyed, tried the customs search and hung up the tow-line. Stopping after one crossing counts.
photoIdea: The cargo toy half-hidden under a towel crate with your dog's nose in close, shot at floor level.
memoryPrompt: What did your dog pick as cargo, and which crate did they search first?
supplies: Three of your dog's own toys
Paper for port signs and the manifest
safety: Only for dogs who enjoy tug and swap willingly; skip it for toy guarders or dogs with neck or back problems.
Keep each tug to 10 to 15 seconds, low and sideways, with light resistance; never yank, lift or shake the toy.
A stiff body, hard grip, fixed stare or intense growl means stop and let them settle; keep children out of it.
